title: Smartsheet Pricing 2026: Plans, Add-Ons, and Costs
summary: Smartsheet pricing structures determine your monthly expenses based on user seats and automation limits. Evaluate these tiers to select the right plan.
body_markdown:
## Smartsheet pricing compared to Monday.com and Asana


Smartsheet positions itself as a mid-market compromise, but the base seat price masks the eventual cost of scaling automation and security.


While the sticker price suggests savings over premium competitors, the functional gap between tiers necessitates earlier upgrades to the Enterprise level than the international math implies.


### Market price comparisons


Smartsheet occupies the middle ground of the project management market when looking at the monthly cost for a 20-person team.[Softr](https://www.softr.io/blog/smartsheet-pricing) lists the monthly seat prices for mid-tier plans as:


Platform Mid-Tier Plan Monthly Seat Price Minimum Seats Monthly Entry Cost


Monday.com Standard 12 USD 3 36 USD


Smartsheet Business 19 USD 3 57 USD


Asana Advanced 24.99 USD 1 24.99 USD


$380 is the base monthly cost for a 20-person team on Smartsheet, sitting between Monday.com ($240) and Asana ($499.80).


### Minimum seat requirements for small teams


The entry price for Smartsheet Business is actually $57 per month because of the **three-seat minimum** .


While Monday.com also enforces a three-seat minimum on its Standard plan, its lower per-seat rate makes the starting cost $36 per month, which means small teams must commit to a higher base expenditure than the per-user price suggests.


A small team of two people will find that Smartsheet Business is more expensive than Asana Advanced, despite Asana having a higher per-seat sticker price. This is because Asana allows teams to pay for exactly what they use, whereas Smartsheet forces a higher price floor.


While Smartsheet appears to save a controller $119.80 per month over Asana for a 20-person team, that margin disappears once the team hits the strict automation caps inherent to the Business tier, rendering the initial price advantage effectively moot for high-volume users, so a company scaling its operations will likely face unexpected upgrade costs.


### Hidden caps on unlimited tiers


The Business tier marketing materials promise unlimited automation, but this label applies only to internal sheet triggers. Any workflow that interacts with external software through the Smartsheet API or premium connectors is subject to the Advance licensing model.


A controller will find that while they can move rows between sheets infinitely, they cannot sync that data to a CRM or ERP without hitting a functional wall.


These cross-platform bridges are gated behind Smartsheet Advance, which effectively reintroduces caps by requiring a higher-tier purchase for external data velocity.


This distinction means the Business tier is only unlimited within the Smartsheet silo. As soon as a team requires a connected tech stack, the "unlimited" promise fails, forcing an upgrade to Enterprise or the purchase of a Silver, Gold, or Platinum Advance package.


### Collaborator limits versus viewer access


A project manager can't share a dashboard with an entire department for active contribution without purchasing additional licenses because the Pro plan limits items to 10 Collaborators. These are individuals who possess the rights to edit, create, or manage the data within the sheets.


While the Pro plan allows for Unlimited viewers who can see the data without changing it, the ceiling on active participants is remarkably low.


A team of eleven people who all need to update their own task status will find themselves forced into the Business tier regardless of their sheet volume.


This tier also restricts automation to 250 workflows per month. A single sheet with three status-change triggers will exhaust this limit in days, halting all background data updates.


### Smartsheet Business vs Enterprise tier comparison


The Business tier introduces unlimited viewers, but it lacks the "Advance" capabilities required for multi-system synchronization.


To connect Smartsheet to a CRM like Salesforce or a developer tool like GitHub, an organization must move to the Enterprise tier or pay for Smartsheet Advance add-ons.


Without these, a controller is left with manual data entry, as the base Business plan doesn't include the connectors needed to maintain a single source of truth across the tech stack.
